calls.head: The Maple Leafs got an upgrade
calls.body: Taken over this season and last, the Maple Leafs are near the bottom of the league for shot volume. Look at this season alone, though, and they’ve been shooting more, around the middle. We think tonight looks more like this season’s Maple Leafs.

calls.head: Bobrovsky’s hold on the Golden Knights won’t last
calls.body: Bobrovsky has been a wall against the Golden Knights since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Bobrovsky isn’t that wall tonight.

calls.head: The Golden Knights’ power play has a target
calls.body: The Golden Knights’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Maple Leafs’ kill is one of the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Maple Leafs more than most.

surprises.head: Toronto hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Toronto usually hits less than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a quiet night on the body: a hit score of 41 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 90 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Stone sparks a Golden Knights comeback
paras: What a comeback. It was a busy first period. Jack Roslovic got the scoring started for the Maple Leafs just 34 seconds into the game, his 300th NHL point. Easton Cowan stretched the lead to 2-0 less than three minutes later, and Nick Paul scored his first goal for Toronto midway through the first to make it 3-0. Mark Stone got the Golden Knights on the board late in the period. Brett Howden cut Toronto’s lead to 3-2 early in the second, and Jack Eichel tied it up on a penalty shot less than three minutes later. The shootout went five rounds, and Trevor Connelly won it for the Golden Knights after Braeden Bowman had scored earlier.

The Golden Knights carried the play, outshooting the Maple Leafs 43-24, but needed a shootout to win it. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Golden Knights win in regulation about seven in ten. Adin Hill settled in after a shaky start for the Golden Knights: he gave up three goals on the first seven shots, then stopped the last 17, and Sergei Bobrovsky made 40 saves in a losing effort.
The Maple Leafs hit two posts and came up a goal short. The Golden Knights improved to 4-1-0, tied for first in the NHL in points. The Leafs fell to 2-2-1, fifth in the Atlantic.
